pr_title: Override Write(Span) for CryptoStream to clear arrays before returning to pool
pr_body:
`CryptoStream` currently takes the stance that it always clears buffers before returning rented buffers to the `ArrayPool`. We do that, except for the base `Stream.Write(ReadOnlySpan<byte> buffer)`. The result of that is that using `Write` will leave data in the ArrayPool when it is rented back out again.

I looked at all other uses of `ArrayPool.Rent` in the base stream. `CryptoStream` is overriding all of them, except this one.

Closes #83295.

issue_context.title: Using CryptoStream leaves copy of unencrypted data in shared array pool after it has been encrypted
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-security, @vcsjones See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description I did report this to MSRC but the report was closed saying "We determined that this behavior is considered to be by design. This behavior is due to how the GC and the runtime works.". So it isn't a vulnerability but I still thought it was unexpected. I would have expected that once my data was encrypted using CryptoStream that my unencrypted data would not be available to rent via ArrayPool. ### Reproduction Steps ```csharp // Simulate getting the data from somewhere and let's say it gets the word "secret" encoded in UTF-8. var data = new byte []{ 0x73, 0x65, 0x63, 0x72, 0x65, 0x74 }; // Ensure we dispose of streams before we try to rent from the array pool. using (var ms = new MemoryStream()) { using (var cs = new CryptoStream(ms, Aes.Create().CreateEncryptor(), CryptoStreamMode.Write)) { cs.Write(data); cs.FlushFinalBlock(); } // Do something with encrypted data in memory stream. } // Ensure my data is cleared from memory after being encrypted. Array.Clear(data); var rental = ArrayPool.Shared.Rent(data.Length); // The line below outputs: Rented from the pool and got secret Console.WriteLine($"Rented from the pool and got {Encoding.UTF8.GetString(rental)}"); ``` ### Expected behavior Renting from the array pool after using CryptoStream would not return my unencrypted data. ### Actual behavior Renting from the array pool after using CryptoStream returns my unencrypted data. ### Regression? _No response_ ### Known Workarounds _No response_ ### Configuration .NET 6 Windows 11 x64 ### Other information _No response_
Author: dev991301
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Security`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

This is actually coming from `Stream` base class:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0f1866ead5aef15d47983692bafb4ba20cd3aa98/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/IO/Stream.cs#L922-L934

The `Write` ends up renting from the pool, converting it to an array, but `Write` doesn't clear what it rented when returning the buffer to the pool.

One way to avoid this is to use the array overload: change your `cs.Write(data);` to `cs.Write(data, 0, data.Length);`. It's only the span overload that rents from the pool. You'll get better performance with this call, too.

We should _probably_ override `public virtual void Write(ReadOnlySpan<byte> buffer)` in `CryptoStream`. If anything, it can do exactly what `Stream` does, except clear when returning to the pool.

@stephentoub I think you had some reservations previously about overriding `Write(ReadOnlySpan<byte> buffer)` in `CryptoStream`. I'm guessing that changing the base `Stream` to clear would be a deal-breaker performance wise. Does overriding this method seem like the appropriate fix here?

> I'm guessing that changing the base Stream to clear would be a deal-breaker performance

Yes

> Does overriding this method seem like the appropriate fix here?

If this is really a problem that needs fixing. You also would presumably care about other places ArrayPool is used with streams, only some of which are in CryptoStream's control, like CopyTo (which it can control for the outgoing direction by overriding it, but obviously not for other streams copying into it). And of course even if you do all that, the incoming data is still on the GC heap and could easily have left shadow copies.

review_comments:
Can this use the [`CryptoPool`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/967250cc86b4c613015066b47b882e7424fdb590/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Security/Cryptography/CryptoPool.cs#L9) instead the ArrayPool?
It does the same thing, but abstracted away via Rent/Return.

No. There are other comments in `CryptoStream` that explain why: we don't rent from `CryptoPool` and give callers access to the array. That includes the virtual `Write`.

Though `CryptoPool` is currently backed by `ArrayPool.Shared`, there is/was an eventual goal that the `CryptoPool` is a separate pool. What we wouldn't want is someone overriding `Write(byte[]...)` and stashing that array and violating the use-after-return expectations of it.
